source.title: Do vision models know that three is three?
source.authors: Ankit Sonthalia; Arnas Uselis; S. Oh

record.file_problem: The paper text appears complete and readable, including its appendix; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports incomplete and concept-dependent cross-regime alignment within vision encoders, while also finding that it tends to increase with local linearity. It frames this as a different form of convergence from the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.
record.gate_note: The study measures concept-direction consistency across visual regimes within individual encoders, not pairwise distances or representation alignment between independently trained models. Its reported correlations and regime-level results bear on partial, input-dependent alignment; it does not test cross-modal image-caption alignment, convergence across seeds, or recurring features across models.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether a concept direction found in one visual regime (e.g., MNIST digits) transfers to another regime (e.g., fingers) within a single encoder. It never compares representations between models, between seeds, or across modalities. The authors call this 'a different form of convergence' from the Platonic Representation Hypothesis and say the result only 'echoes' it. This is a related but different construct, so it tests no version. The local–global correlations are computed across 46 models, but they relate two within-model properties, not alignment between models.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress that the local–global correlation is a trend in current models and not a causal effect. They frame it as echoing, not testing, the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, and they leave open whether regime-specific skills converge into abstract ones.
record.recipe_differences: Measures within-encoder directional consistency across visual regimes using cosine alignment of concept displacements and random baselines. It does not use the Platonic Representation Hypothesis's cross-model comparison of representations or distances.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by concept and regime; fragmentation also differs between the reported supervised ViT and CLIP examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a single vision encoder, concept directions are locally linear in nearly all regimes (99.1% significant). Cross-regime transfer is significant in only 52.2% of tests and varies by concept, from 18.3% (dry→wet) to 99.3% (dog→horse). Supervised models fragment more than CLIP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model cross-domain concept convergence: a single vision model encodes the same abstract concept with a shared direction across visually distinct regimes.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 46 models, global (cross-regime) linearity rises with local linearity (Kendall tau 0.38–0.89). Cross-regime probe accuracy rises with global linearity (tau 0.53–0.77).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models with stronger local concept structure have more regime-invariant concept geometry.

record.problems: The paper states that its counterfactual pairs are approximate and matched by embedding-space distance, and that conclusions are limited to the investigated concept types. Results primarily use statistical significance rates, which do not by themselves report the magnitude of alignment. The study does not measure cross-model pairwise representation distances, model capability scaling, or causal effects.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No alignment between independently trained models; no analysis by model size or capability.
No mapping, stitching or relative representations between models; probes transfer across regimes within one model.
No test of features or circuits recurring across models.
No cross-model convergence measure, so no test of metric or data dependence of convergence.
No cross-model alignment level, plateau, or causal attribution to shared data or objectives.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V6 and V7 and gave labels. That is not justified: V6 and V7 concern alignment between models, while every measure here is within a single model across input regimes. The verdict is reclassified to discusses/T6 and the findings are moved to fits_no_version. The model list spans scales (e.g., CLIP RN50 to ViT-bigG), but no result is reported by size.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure alignment between independently trained models as model size or capability increases.
Does not compare image and caption representations or measure cross-modal alignment as model performance changes.
Does not compare models trained from different initializations or identify shared features or subspaces across seeds.
Tests directions transferring across visual regimes within one encoder, not mappings between different models, stitching, relative representations, or transfer without paired data.
Does not test whether interpretable features or circuits recur across models.

Tests variation across concepts and visual regimes using direction-consistency measures. Does not compare alternative similarity metrics or settings such as neighbour counts, and does not test out-of-distribution inputs.
Finds incomplete and variable cross-regime alignment, but does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause it, nor whether alignment plateaus with scale or capability.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across tested concept families and regimes
reader_labels.reason: Cross-regime significance rates vary substantially by concept (18.3%–99.3%), so the measured alignment depends on which concepts and regimes are evaluated; see r14, r16, r18, r20, r22, r24, r26, r28, r30, and r32.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Numerosity and cleanliness; supervised ViT examples
reader_labels.reason: Cross-regime direction consistency is near baseline for many pairs despite significant local consistency, showing fragmented rather than complete alignment; see r33 and r35.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across tested models and concepts, especially object identity and age
reader_labels.reason: Global consistency is not uniformly absent: it is statistically above baseline in most tested pairs for dog→horse and young→old, and global consistency increases with local linearity across every concept; see r3–r12 and r30, r32.
